idiom_name: handler middleware closure + cached lookup func + singleflight coalescing
implementation_notes: Go has no integration framework and needs none: enrichment is middleware that wraps the message handler (or the http.Handler), resolves the key, fetches the missing fields and passes the enriched struct to the next stage - the classic Enricher component collapses into a closure over a lookup function. context.Context carries the deadline and cancellation into the resource call, and golang.org/x/sync/singleflight collapses identical concurrent lookups so a burst of messages about one customer issues one query; a bounded map or LRU in front of the source covers the repeat case. Keep the source behind a small interface so tests substitute a stub.
pitfalls: singleflight only deduplicates overlapping calls; without a cache every later message still hits the resource once the window closes.
Caching pointers to shared structs invites data races when a later stage mutates the message - cache immutable copies (or return values) instead.
Without a context deadline a slow resource parks the handler goroutine indefinitely; pass ctx and wrap the client call with a timeout.
